mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 2.0% (FEDFUNDS < 2.0%) signals an accommodative monetary policy that lowers discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 2.0% over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate exceeding 5.5% (UNRATE > 5.5%) indicates deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE > 5.5% over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO < 100) and housing starts (HOUST < 900) indicates a broad-based contraction in real economic output, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when both INDPRO < 100 and HOUST < 900 over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate exceeding 4.0% (FEDFUNDS > 4.0%) during a monetary tightening cycle signals increased borrowing costs that reduce corporate investment and equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.0% over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A GDP level below 16000 billion dollars (GDPC1 < 16000) indicates a contractionary economic environment that reduces corporate revenue growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when GDPC1 < 16000 over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A high level of real sales (RSAFS > 350000) reflects robust consumer spending that supports corporate earnings growth, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when RSAFS > 350000 over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A CPIAUCSL index above 220.0 indicates elevated inflation that prompts Federal Reserve tightening, reducing equity valuations and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 220.0 over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in payroll employment (PAYEMS < 137000) and rise in unemployment (UNRATE > 6.0%) indicates severe labor market contraction that reduces household income and consumer spending, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when PAYEMS < 137000 and UNRATE > 6.0% over a 5-year rolling window.
